name: NY-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+33 partisan lean makes a Republican win nearly impossible
Lasher's overwhelming money edge: $3.3M raised plus $10.8M outside support vs. $155K for Shinkle
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 99%
Open seat with no general-election polling adds modest uncertainty about the margin
model.rationale: The district's deep Democratic lean, Lasher's lopsided financial advantage, and near-certain market pricing leave Shinkle without a realistic path; the open seat and lack of polling only cloud the size of the win, not the outcome.
model.watch: A sharply unfavorable national environment for Democrats or very low turnout could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would require an unprecedented shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jerry Nadler (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New York's 12th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, and Jerry Nadler's retirement hands an open, heavily blue district to the Democratic side in all likelihood. Micah Lasher has raised more than $3.3 million and drawn over $10.7 million in outside support, dwarfing the roughly $155,000 collected by Republican Caroline Shinkle. Prediction markets put the odds of a Democratic win near certainty.

The main uncertainty is the absence of any general-election polling and the open-seat dynamic, which can compress margins in low-information races. Two minor-party candidates are on the ballot but have raised little money. The district's fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic victory, with the open question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
